subject: Approval request: Regional failover automation game day (staging) — scope + go/no-go
body:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Approval request: Regional failover automation game day (staging) — scope + go/no-go

Neha / Priya — requesting approval to run the first controlled failover automation game day in staging.

Proposed window
- Tue 2/18 10:00–11:30am PT (staging only)

Objective
- Validate trigger evaluation + orchestrator state machine end-to-end under controlled impairment
- Validate safety guards (capacity/dependency gates + hold-down timers) and manual override
- Collect data to tune thresholds before any prod test

Scope / blast radius
- Environment: staging
- Traffic: perf-canary + internal load only (no customer traffic)
- Routes/models: chat + embeddings (staging equivalents), single region pair us-west-2 → us-east-1
- Progressive failover enabled (10% → 25% → 50% canary steps), rollback available at any stage

Risk controls (high level)
- Feature flag remains OFF by default; we explicitly enable for game day and disable at end
- Orchestrator in "monitor + recommend" for first 10 minutes; then we allow automated transition under IC approval
- Safe-to-failover gates must pass:
  - Target region headroom >= 25% GPU pool (staging)
  - Queue depth not increasing; no dependency incidents on shared services
  - Routing policy sanity check passes (no conflicting pinned versions)
- Hysteresis: 5m evaluation window, 15m hold-down timer to prevent flapping
- Manual override + kill switch available to IC and on-call

Go/No-Go (staging)
GO if:
- Capacity check passes in target region
- DNS/edge TTL and routing policy change path verified (dry run)
- On-call staffed: IC + scribe + platform observer + infra observer
NO-GO if:
- Any active incident on staging control plane/routing
- Any capacity signal is missing/unknown for either region
- perf-canary is already failing (baseline red)

Docs
- Confluence plan (roles, steps, stop conditions): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGSRE/Controlled+Failover+Game+Day+Plan+2025Q2
- Drive checklist (pre-flight + post-flight): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1rwd-staging-gameday-checklist

If approved today, we’ll schedule and post a heads-up in #announcements and #eng-oncall.

Thanks,
Sean
Director, SRE
Redwood Inference


From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 9:34 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: Regional failover automation game day (staging) — scope + go/no-go

+1 to doing this in staging first.

Two asks before I sign off:
1) Confirm the routing policy store writes are behind the same flag (i.e., no “partial enable” where the trigger flips state but routing doesn’t update cleanly).
2) What is the explicit stop condition if we see cascading retries / elevated 99p latency in the target region during the ramp (even if error rate stays low)?

Also, please include Connor explicitly as approver for any DNS/edge changes even in staging—just want the muscle memory.

Priya


From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 10:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: Regional failover automation game day (staging) — scope + go/no-go

All fair.

1) Routing policy store writes
- Yes: the orchestrator transition that would change routing is gated behind the same flag + an explicit “allow-actuation” toggle in staging.
- In the monitor-only phase, it will compute the next state and emit an audit event but will not write to routing policy.
- We’ll do a dry-run step to validate policy write + rollback endpoints before any induced impairment.

2) Stop condition for latency/retry amplification
We’ll treat this as a hard stop (rollback) if any of the following are observed for >3 minutes during a ramp step:
- p99 latency in target region increases >30% vs pre-test baseline AND concurrent request count increases (suggests queueing)
- Retry rate >2x baseline OR upstream 429/503 from shared dependencies (auth, quota, policy store)
- Queue depth slope positive for 2 consecutive 1-min intervals

Plan update: we’ll add this to the “STOP CONDITIONS” section in Confluence and the checklist.

Connor — agree. We can add a checkbox requiring your go-ahead before any DNS/edge-related action (even if it’s just confirming we’re only doing internal routing changes).

Sean


From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 11:06 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: Regional failover automation game day (staging) — scope + go/no-go

Approved for staging on Tue 2/18 with the guardrails as written + Priya’s additions.

Conditions:
- Keep it strictly staging/internal load; no exceptions.
- IC must have a single “kill switch” step documented and rehearsed in the first 10 minutes.
- Capture a short readout after (what triggered, what didn’t, any noisy signals, and what we’ll change before prod).

Connor: please confirm in-thread once you’re comfortable with the change path (even if DNS/edge isn’t touched, I want the sign-off loop).

Talia: please ensure the roles are assigned by EOD Monday and that we post a heads-up in #announcements with the exact window.

Thanks,
Neha
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability
Redwood Inference
